properties.name: immutable installs
properties.verbatim:
installs are immutable and content-addressed/versioned; activation never
  mutates verified bytes in place;
properties.obligation: A generation's verified bytes are never rewritten in place. Activation publishes a new generation or fails. In-place mutation is a failed successor.

properties.name: lock pin set
properties.verbatim:
project locks select exact signed index snapshot, component/artifact closure,
  platform alternative, subprotocol/state formats, and policy constraints;
properties.t2Decision: The lock PINS those five. A live handshake may only CONFIRM that the running process matches the pin. Handshake MUST NOT substitute, widen, or renegotiate a pinned subprotocol/state format. Window meaning of those format identifiers is DR-111's (ID-DEP-G3).

properties.name: operation pins generation for its lifetime
properties.verbatim: each operation pins the project-selected generation for its entire lifetime;
properties.obligation: An operation's generation cannot change under it. A later project lock change starts a new operation, never mutates a live one.

properties.name: concurrent conflicting project selections
properties.verbatim: different projects may concurrently select conflicting component versions;
properties.obligation: Two projects may hold incompatible closures at the same time. Their generations must not mix. A process leased to generation A cannot observe generation B's bytes as if they were A's.

properties.name: leases/refcounts
properties.verbatim:
active processes hold generation leases/refcounts and open references needed
  for safe completion/recovery;
properties.obligation: A live process holds a lease on its generation. Crash recovery consults leases. Lease release is explicit or process-death reaped. A lease is not a secret and not a trust decision.

properties.name: reference-safe GC/removal
properties.verbatim:
remove and GC cannot delete bytes/state referenced by locks, active processes,
  retained evidence, rollback slots, or prepared migrations;
properties.obligation: Deletion is eligible only when reachabilityRoots is empty for that generation. Removal deactivates; it does not invent a typed purge result (ID-DEP-G4).

properties.name: atomic old-or-new publication
properties.verbatim:
activation atomically publishes the dependency, permission/confinement,
  executable, schema, state, and migration closure; observers see old or new,
  never a mixture; and
properties.obligation: Observers of a project see generation N or generation N+1, never a mix of dependency, permission, executable, schema, state, or migration halves.

properties.name: monotonic trust state separate from executables
properties.verbatim:
trust roots, revocation observations, expiry floors, and anti-rollback counters
  are separate monotonic state and never roll back with executable pointers.
properties.obligation: Rolling back a generation MUST NOT roll back trust/revocation/expiry/anti-rollback state. The state machine for those values is DR-112's. This property is the join: executable pointers and trust counters are distinct stores.

steps.verbatim: prepare builds and verifies complete target state without changing authority;
steps.obligation: Prepare has no observer-visible authority change.

steps.verbatim:
commit atomically publishes the new generation/schema after required readers
  and custody are available;
steps.obligation: Commit is the P-7 publication act.

steps.verbatim: abort leaves old authoritative state intact and inventories/cleans target;
steps.obligation: Abort is not a trust rollback (P-8).

steps.verbatim:
each migration declares backward-read support, write format, rollback window,
  and any no-return boundary; and
steps.obligation: Those four declarations are required data. Their compatibility meaning is DR-111's.

steps.verbatim:
repair media is signed and checked against current roots/revocation/expiry;
  repair never rolls security state backward.
steps.obligation: Repair-media shipping is DR-110. This property is the join: repair cannot violate P-8. Preview does not author a self-update harness (D-002 / G18 scopeRider).

rules: Every lifecycle operation is journaled and lease-scoped.
Publication requires durable staged files/directories/journal, same-filesystem atomic rename or a reviewed equivalent, and recovery at each write/fsync/rename/pointer transition.
After a crash, ambiguous bytes or state fail closed and quarantine.
Recovery may resume or restore only an exact verified generation permitted by current trust.
crashSafety.doesNotChoose: The reviewed equivalent of atomic rename is reserved. Fail-closed quarantine is required; the on-disk quarantine format is reserved.
